context: Queue task 324, GH#624, stage S5. Design APPROVED by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (commit d8a4dd3) after two rework rounds -- the fail-uninterceptability mechanism was independently live-verified against real wasmex 0.15.1: exit/1 inside a host callback does NOT crash the Wasmex instance process (caught by handle_info/2's catch clause); wasmex's Rust NIF discards the failure reason and substitutes one fixed generic message identical for exit/raise/throw; do_fail/5 must stash %{reason:, details:} into its own process dictionary via Process.put/2 immediately before exit/1, readable via Process.info(pid, :dictionary) from PluginHandler's process strictly BEFORE the existing unconditional GenServer.stop/1 in run_guest/3 tears the instance down -- read call_export/3 in lib/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler.ex to see exactly where that stop call happens and where your check must run before it. Read the full design doc before writing any code -- it is the authority for exact identifiers, ordering, and the shared parity harness shape. Read lib/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api.ex (REQ-171 sibling, read path) for the existing module's structure/conventions to extend. Read lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex's write_variable/call_service/fail for the Lua semantics you must match at parity -- decision 0014 Decision (4): Lua is the definition, do not modify it.

task.description: Implement REQ-172 exactly as designed in lib/letflow/design/req172-wasm-host-api-write-path-and-parity-suite.md: add do_write_variable/*, do_call_service/*, do_fail/5 to lib/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api.ex (or as the design specifies); extend lib/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler.ex's call_export/3 to check the fail-signal process-dictionary key before GenServer.stop/1 runs; add the shared parity harness (Letflow.Test.HostApiParity or as named in the design) under test/support/; add CapabilityGate.known_host_functions/0 if the design calls for it. Implement write_variable's staging/atomic-apply-on-success/discard-on-every-failure-arm semantics exactly as designed. Implement call_service's two distinct failure paths (structured error return on service failure vs. instantiation-time capability denial). Do NOT modify any file under lib/letflow/engine/lua/ -- Lua is the definition, WASM conforms to it. Do not write test files yet (that is TEST-DESIGNER's step) beyond what the design specifies as your own deliverable (e.g. the shared parity harness support module, if the design assigns that to you rather than TEST-DESIGNER -- check the design's Deliverables Summary). Run mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test yourself and quote real output; do not claim success without running it.
acceptance_criteria: write_variable stages writes and discards them on every failure arm (guest trap, REQ-169 fuel exhaustion, REQ-169 memory cap, REQ-170 wall-clock timeout, fail), applying atomically only on success, per the design's exact mechanism
call_service returns a structured error to the guest on service failure (never traps) while a missing capability fails at instantiation per REQ-167 -- the two paths structurally distinct

fail terminates via the design's live-verified pdict-stash-then-exit mechanism, checked by call_export/3 strictly before GenServer.stop/1, so a guest cannot catch or ignore it and it does not run to completion
the shared parity harness deliverable (per the design's Deliverables Summary) is implemented as designed
no file under lib/letflow/engine/lua/ is modified
mix compile --warnings-as-errors passes with real output quoted
mix test passes with real output quoted (existing suite; new tests are TEST-DESIGNER's step)
